blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: As agents powered by foundation models move into open-ended environments, continual learning from experience becomes essential. For agents built on models with fixed parameters, this learning requires reusing prior task experience in context to improve performance and efficiency on future tasks. Existing memory and experience-learning systems typically focus on either retained facts or procedures, and lack a mechanism for establishing the reliability of claims extracted from the ongoing task stream. Indeed, we find that approximately 12--33\% of entries produced by representative systems harm future task performance when reused. To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{RIKA} (Reliable Knowledge Acquisition), which combines hierarchical extraction of factual, conceptual, procedural, and metacognitive knowledge with Evidence-based Knowledge Admission, which uses source evidence and subsequent experience to govern which claims enter the task agent's context, without additional validation tasks. Across six task streams from Continual Learning Bench and four model backbones, RIKA achieves the highest aggregate score on every backbone.
blocks.zh: 随着基础模型的推动因素进入开放环境,不断从经验中学习变得至关重要。 对于基于有固定参数的模型的代理人来说,这种学习需要重新利用以前的任务经验,以提高未来任务的业绩和效率。 现有的记忆和经验学习系统通常侧重于保留的事实或程序,缺乏一种机制来确定从目前的任务流中提取的索赔的可靠性。 事实上,我们发现,在代表系统制作的条目中,大约有12-33分左右的条目在重复使用时会损害未来的任务性能。 为解决这些局限性,我们提议\textbf{RIKA}(可靠知识获取),将事实知识、概念知识、程序性知识和元认知知识的分级提取与基于证据的知识获取结合起来,利用来源证据和随后的经验来规范声称进入任务代理背景的情况,而不增加验证任务。 在连续学习班的6个任务流和4个示范骨干中,RIKA在每个骨干中取得了最高的总分.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Foundation-model agents increasingly operate in open-ended environments, where they encounter ongoing streams of tasks whose demands cannot be fully anticipated during training ( Zhang et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2024 ; Shu et al., 2026 ; Zheng et al., 2025 ) . Their experience provides a continuing source of learning (e.g., lessons from failures). For agents built on black-box language models with fixed parameters, this learning takes place through context: knowledge acquired from prior trajectories is supplied to guide subsequent decisions ( Shinn et al., 2023 ) . Continual learning therefore requires organizing past experience into reusable knowledge that can inform future tasks.
blocks.zh: 基金会的模型代理人越来越多地在不限名额的环境中运作,在这种环境中,他们不断遇到各种任务,在培训期间无法充分预料这些任务的需求(Zhang等人,2025年;Liu等人,2000年)。 2024; Shu等, 2026; Zheng等, 2025). 他们的经验提供了持续的学习来源(例如,失败的教训)。 对于基于有固定参数的黑盒语言模型的代理,这种学习通过上下文进行: 提供从前作轨迹获得的知识来指导后作决定(Shinn等,2023.). 因此,继续学习需要将过去的经验组织成可重复使用的知识,为今后的任务提供信息。

blocks.en:
A central challenge in reusing experience is whether extracted knowledge can be trusted to guide future decisions .
Existing memory systems ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026 ) often lack an explicit mechanism accounting for the reliability of extracted knowledge.
Some experience-learning systems validate extracted knowledge by replaying tasks ( Li et al., 2026 ) or evaluating on held-out tasks ( Yang et al., 2026b ) , both of which require additional task execution that may be unavailable in continual settings, where environment states cannot be revisited or reset.
Our quantitative evaluation of artifacts produced by representative systems shows that approximately 12–33% of evaluated atomic claims reduce subsequent task performance when reused.
A complementary qualitative case study further reveals how such failures arise. Extracted knowledge may rely on information unavailable at reuse time, mismatch the requirements of subsequent tasks, or become outdated as the environment changes (Section 3.1 ).
blocks.zh:
重新利用经验的一个主要挑战是,是否可以相信所获取的知识来指导今后的决策。
现有的记忆系统(Chhikara等,2025;Xu等,2026;Liu等,2026)往往缺乏明确的机制,无法说明所取知识的可靠性.
一些经验学习系统通过重放任务(Li等,2026年)或评价被搁置任务(Yang等,2026年b)验证所取出的知识,两者都需要额外任务执行,在持续环境下可能无法执行,环境状态无法被重温或重置.
我们对代表性系统所生产文物的定量评价表明,在评估的原子索赔中,大约有12-33%在再利用时降低了随后的任务性能。
一项补充性的质量案例研究进一步揭示了这种失败是如何发生的。 所取出的知识可能依赖在再利用时无法获得的信息,不符合后续任务的要求,或随着环境的变化而过时(第3.1节)。

blocks.en: Beyond reliability, continual learning also requires deciding what knowledge to acquire . Memory systems mostly retain facts and events, while experience-learning systems distill skills, workflows, reflections, and strategic guidance ( Wang et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2026b ; Ni et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026b ; Shinn et al., 2023 ) . Beyond observations and procedures, agents also need to learn underlying principles and when to apply or revise a method. This motivates a structured approach to learning complementary forms of knowledge and organizing the relationships among them.
blocks.zh: 除了可靠性之外,继续学习还需要决定获得何种知识。 记忆系统大多保留了事实和事件,而经验学习系统则分泌出技能,工作流程,反思和战略指导(王等,2024;张等,2026b;倪等,2026;杨等,2026b;申等,2023. 除了观察和程序之外,代理人还需要学习基本原则,以及何时适用或修订某种方法。 这促使采取有条理的办法,学习补充性的知识并组织它们之间的关系。

blocks.en: To address these two challenges, we propose RIKA ( R el i able K nowledge A cquisition), a continual learning framework that transforms agents’ task experience into structured knowledge for future decisions. To ensure reliable reuse, RIKA introduces Evidence-based Knowledge Admission (EKA) , which draws on sequential hypothesis testing and truth maintenance ( Wald, 1992 ; Doyle, 1979 ) to admit and revise atomic claims as evidence accumulates from the ongoing task stream. Claims directly established by their source trajectories can be admitted immediately, while those requiring broader support remain pending until sufficient evidence accumulates; subsequent experience can also challenge earlier admissions. This process requires no additional validation tasks. For knowledge extraction, RIKA draws on a knowledge taxonomy from educational psychology ( Anderson and Krathwohl, 2001 ) to acquire four complementary types of knowledge: factual, conceptual, procedural, and metacognitive. Its hierarchical extractor grounds conceptual abstractions in factual knowledge and metacognitive abstractions in procedural knowledge, organizing both concrete experience and higher-level understanding for reuse.
blocks.zh: 为了应对这两项挑战,我们提议建立Rika(R i able K nowledge A Cquisition),这是一个不断学习的框架,将代理人员的任务经验转化为结构化的知识,供今后决策之用。 为了确保可靠的再利用,RIKA采用了基于证据的知识接纳(EKA),它利用相继的假说测试和真理维护(Wald,1992年;Doyle,1979年),承认并修订原子权利主张,作为从目前任务流积累的证据。 直接由其来源轨迹确定的索赔可以立即受理,而那些需要更广泛支持的索赔则有待于充分的证据积累;随后的经验也可以对先前的受理提出质疑。 这一过程不需要额外的验证任务. 关于知识取出,RIKA利用教育心理学的知识分类学(Anderson和Krathwohl,2001年)获得四种互补的知识:事实、概念、程序和元认知。 它的分级提取器为事实知识中的概念抽象和程序性知识中的元认知抽象提供了依据,组织具体的经验和更高层次的再利用理解.

blocks.en: Our contributions are threefold: • We identify and quantify a reliability problem in experience reuse, finding that approximately 12–33% of evaluated entries from representative systems harm subsequent task performance. • We propose RIKA, combining evidence-based knowledge admission with hierarchical extraction of factual, conceptual, procedural, and metacognitive knowledge. • We demonstrate RIKA’s effectiveness across different task streams and model backbones, achieving the highest aggregate score on all backbones.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Memory for Agents
blocks.zh: 2.1 代理人记忆

blocks.en: Agent memory systems maintain information from prior interactions for later use. Much of this work is rooted in conversational personal assistants, where memory centers on past events, personal information, and user preferences ( Maharana et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2024 ; Hu et al., 2026b ) . These systems develop memory storage, extraction, and organization mechanisms to retain and retrieve information across interactions ( Sumers et al., 2023 ; Zhong et al., 2024 ; Packer et al., 2023 ; Chhikara et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026 ) . Together, these efforts help agents preserve relevant context across interactions.
blocks.zh: 代理内存系统从先前的相互作用中保存信息供后用. 大部分作品植根于对话个人助手,记忆中心是过去的事件、个人信息和用户偏好(Maharana等,2024;Wu等,2024;Hu等,2026b)。 这些系统发展了存储、提取和组织机制,以保留和取回跨越相互作用的信息(Sumers等,2023;Zhong等,2024;Packer等,2023;Chhikara等,2025;Xu等,2026;Liu等,2026)。 这些努力共同帮助各行为者在互动中保持相关背景。

blocks.en: 2.2 Learning from Task Experience
blocks.zh: 2.2 从任务经验中学习

blocks.en: Another line of work extracts reusable knowledge from task experience. Some approaches distill experience into executable skills ( Wang et al., 2023 ; Ni et al., 2026 ) , action workflows ( Wang et al., 2024 ) , reflections ( Shinn et al., 2023 ) , reasoning insights ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) , and playbooks ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) . While several methods validate acquired knowledge before reuse, they rely on replaying tasks or evaluating on held-out tasks ( Alzubi et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026b ) , which requires additional task execution that is costly and often infeasible once the environment changes. In contrast, our method assesses knowledge using evidence from the ongoing task stream.
blocks.zh: 另一行工作从任务经验中提取了可再利用的知识。 一些方法将经验分解为可执行技能(Wang等,2023;Ni等,2026),动作工作流程(Wang等,2024),反思. (新浪等,2023). 推理洞察 (欧阳等,2026). 和玩本 (张等,2026b. 虽然有几种方法在再利用之前验证已获得的知识,但它们依靠重放任务或评价被搁置的任务(Alzubi等,2026;Li等,2026;Yang等,2026b),这需要额外的任务执行,一旦环境发生变化,任务执行成本高昂,往往不可行. 与此相反,我们的方法利用当前任务流中的证据评估知识。

blocks.en: 2.3 Reliability of Agentic Memory
blocks.zh: 2.3 代理记忆的可靠性

blocks.en: The reliability of stored knowledge can deteriorate as agents accumulate experience. Recent studies identify errors introduced by repeated consolidation ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) , stale knowledge under environmental change ( Chao et al., 2026 ) , and failures when agents consume conflicting memories ( Chen et al., 2026 ) . Complementary empirical work examines how memory management affects agents’ experience-following behavior ( Xiong et al., 2026 ) . Beyond characterizing these risks, TrustMem evaluates memory updates for coverage, preservation, and faithfulness, and uses preference-guided reinforcement learning to improve consolidation ( Yang et al., 2026a ) . Our work focuses on assessing the reliability of extracted knowledge using evidence from the ongoing task stream.
blocks.zh: 随着物剂积累经验,存储知识的可靠性会恶化. 最近的研究找出了反复合并引起的错误(张等,2026a.),在环境变化下的沉淀知识(Chao等,2026.),以及物剂消耗相冲突记忆时的失败(Chen等,2026. 补充的经验性工作审查了记忆管理如何影响代理人的经验跟踪行为(Xiong等,2026年). 除了描述这些风险外,TrustMem还评估了覆盖、保存和忠诚度的记忆更新,并使用偏好指导的强化学习来改进整合(Yang等,2026a.)。 我们的工作重点是评估利用当前工作流中的证据获取的知识的可靠性。

blocks.en: 3 Reliability of Knowledge Extraction in Existing Systems
blocks.zh: 3 现有系统中知识挖掘的可靠性

blocks.en: We first diagnose reliability failures in artifacts produced by four representative systems: Mem0 ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) , ACE ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) , Trace2Skill ( Ni et al., 2026 ) , and SkillOpt ( Yang et al., 2026b ) . We then introduce EKA to govern knowledge reuse and evaluate it with the SkillOpt and Trace2Skill extractors. All analyses in this section useDeepSeek-V4-Flash ( DeepSeek-AI, 2026 ) on three task streams ( DB , Cohort , and Codebase ) from Continual Learning Bench ( Asawa et al., 2026 ) (Section 5.1 ).
blocks.zh: 我们首先诊断出四个具有代表性的系统生产的文物的可靠性故障: Mem0(Chhikara等,2025年),ACE(Zhang等,2026年b),Trace2Skill (Ni等人,2026年),和斯克特 Opt (杨等, 2026b.). 然后我们引入EKA来管理知识的再利用,并用SkillOpt和Trace2Skill提取器来评价它. 本节中的所有分析都使用从连续学习班(Asawa等,2026年)(第5.1节)收到的三个任务流(DB、Cohort和Codebase)的DeepSeek-V4-Flash(DeepSeek-AI,2026年)。

blocks.en: 3.1 How Reliable Is Extracted Knowledge?
blocks.zh: 3.1 知识如何可靠?

blocks.en: We examine the reliability of extracted knowledge through a leave-one-entry-out evaluation. Specifically, we remove one knowledge entry at a time and compare downstream task performance with and without that entry. This allows us to identify harmful entries, whose inclusion significantly degrades performance on subsequent tasks.
blocks.zh: 我们通过 " 一出门 " 评估审查所取知识的可靠性。 具体地说,我们一次删除一个知识条目,并将下游任务业绩与该条目进行比较。 这使得我们可以确定有害条目,列入有害条目将极大地降低后续任务的业绩。

blocks.en: To understand how such failures arise, we compare claims extracted by these systems with their source trajectories and the requirements of subsequent tasks. Figure 1 presents four representative cases. Extracted knowledge may rely on information unavailable at reuse time, mismatch the requirements of subsequent tasks, or become outdated as the environment changes.

blocks.en: Together, these findings show that extraction and admission should be treated separately: a plausible claim is not necessarily reliable enough to guide future decisions. This motivates mechanisms for deciding which knowledge to admit and revising those decisions as new evidence accumulates.
blocks.zh: 这些调查结果加在一起表明,提取和承认应分别处理:合理的说法不一定可靠,足以指导今后的决定。 这促使人们建立机制,决定哪些知识能够作为新证据接受和修订这些决定。

blocks.en: 3.2 Evidence-Based Knowledge Admission
blocks.zh: 3.2 循证知识的接受

blocks.en: We introduce Evidence-based Knowledge Admission (EKA) to govern reuse through evidence. EKA distinguishes claims by whether environment feedback in their source trajectories already establishes them. A claim directly verified by such feedback can be admitted immediately. For example, after an agent inspects a database schema, the claim “in schema version 1, order amounts are stored in orders.amount ” is confirmed by the inspection output. In contrast, a claim that generalizes beyond what was observed remains pending until corroborated by subsequent experience. For example, the rule “for realized-revenue queries, pending orders do not contribute to revenue” is inferred from the records seen in a single task, so it is admitted or rejected only after further evidence emerges. The ongoing task stream thus serves as a source of both knowledge and evidence for its reuse. EKA encompasses atomization, claim routing, relation judgment, evidence accumulation, admission and forgetting, and rendering for reuse (Section 4.4 ).
blocks.zh: 我们采用基于证据的知识招生(EKA)来管理通过证据的再利用. EKA通过源轨迹中的环境反馈是否已经确立来区分索赔. 可通过这种反馈直接核实的索赔可立即予以受理。 例如,在代理人检查了数据库计划之后,“在计划第1版中,订单数额以订单的形式储存......amount......”的索赔得到检查产出的确认。 与此相反,关于超出观察到的范围的概括性的说法仍有待于以后的经验证实。 例如,从一项单一任务中看到的记录中推断出“对已实现收益的查询,待发命令不会增加收入”的规则,因此只有在出现进一步的证据后才予以承认或拒绝。 因此,进行中的任务流既是知识的来源,也是其再利用的证据。 EKA包括原子分解、索赔路线、关系判断、证据积累、承认和遗忘以及再利用(第4.4节)。

blocks.zh: 4 方法

blocks.en: RIKA combines hierarchical knowledge extraction with EKA (Figure 2 ). The extractor acquires four complementary types of knowledge; EKA processes its outputs through atomization, routing, relation judgment, evidence accumulation, admission and forgetting, and rendering for reuse.

blocks.en: 4.1 Setup: Continual Learning from Task Streams
blocks.zh: 4.1 设置: 从任务流中持续学习

blocks.en: We consider a task agent that interacts with an environment over a stream of tasks 𝒯 = { x 1 , … , x T } . \mathcal{T}=\{x_{1},\ldots,x_{T}\}.
blocks.zh: 我们考虑一个任务代理, 通过一系列任务与环境交互 T = { x 1, ..., x T }.\ mathcal{ T}=\{x_{1},\ ldots, x_{T}\}} 。

blocks.en: Solving task x t x_{t} produces a trajectory τ t \tau_{t} consisting of the agent’s actions, environment observations, and feedback. We focus on agents built on black-box models whose parameters remain fixed; continual learning therefore occurs through reusable knowledge acquired from past trajectories and supplied in context for future tasks. blocks.en: 4.2 Knowledge Representation
blocks.zh: 4.2 知识代表性

blocks.en: Inspired by a knowledge taxonomy from educational psychology ( Anderson and Krathwohl, 2001 ) , we represent task experience using four complementary knowledge types, illustrated below with examples from the DB task. Factual knowledge captures task-relevant properties of entities, states, and outcomes (e.g., “ fdbk_g1.ts stores Unix timestamps in milliseconds”). Conceptual knowledge captures relations or regularities that organize multiple facts (e.g., “timestamp encodings differ across feedback tables: milliseconds, seconds, or ISO date strings”). Procedural knowledge specifies executable methods or workflows (e.g., “to filter by a top-level category, use cat_lvl = 1 AND cat_nm = ’<Category>’ ”). Metacognitive knowledge concerns when to apply, select, or revise a method (e.g., “when a category filter returns unexpected results, verify the hierarchy level before revising the query”).
blocks.zh: 在教育心理学知识分类学的启发下(Anderson和Krathwohl,2001年),我们利用四种互补的知识类型代表了任务经验,下文举例说明了发展银行任务的实例。 事实知识捕捉到实体、状态和结果与任务相关的属性(例如“fdbk_g1.ts存储以毫秒为单位的Unix时间戳”). 概念知识能捕捉组织多种事实的关系或规律(例如,“时间戳编码因反馈表而异:毫秒、秒或ISO日期字符串”)。 程序知识规定了可执行的方法或工作流程(例如,“通过顶级类别过滤,使用cat_lvl = 1和cat_nm = QQCategory = ). 元认知知识在何时应用、选择或修改某一方法(例如,“当一个类别过滤器返回出乎意料的结果时,在修改查询之前核实等级级别”)。

blocks.en: 4.3 Hierarchical Knowledge Extraction
blocks.zh: 4.3 分级知识提取

blocks.en: The four knowledge types differ in their level of abstraction ( Anderson and Krathwohl, 2001 ) . Factual and procedural knowledge describe concrete observations and task-solving operations ( Anderson, 1982 ) , which can be directly grounded in environment feedback and agent trajectories. In contrast, conceptual and metacognitive knowledge capture higher-level regularities and strategic judgment ( Nelson, 1990 ) , which typically require further abstraction over factual and procedural knowledge, respectively. We therefore organize knowledge extraction into two stages: first extracting factual and procedural knowledge, and then deriving abstract conceptual and metacognitive knowledge from them, respectively.
blocks.zh: 这四种知识类型在抽象程度上有所不同(Anderson和Krathwohl,2001.)。 事实与程序知识描述了具体的观察和任务解决操作(Anderson, 1982),这些操作可以直接基于环境反馈和代理轨迹. 与此相反,概念知识和元认知知识捕捉到更高层次的规律性和战略判断(Nelson,1990年),这通常要求进一步抽象,分别超越事实知识和程序知识。 因此,我们把知识的取出分为两个阶段:首先取出事实知识和程序知识,然后分别取出抽象的概念知识和元认知知识。

blocks.en: 4.4 Evidence-Based Knowledge Admission (EKA)
blocks.zh: 4.4 循证知识招生

blocks.en: EKA evaluates claims from the ongoing task stream. Inspired by sequential hypothesis testing ( Wald, 1992 ) and truth maintenance ( Doyle, 1979 ) , we keep eligible but insufficiently corroborated claims pending and update their evidence as subsequent trajectories provide support or opposition. EKA proceeds through stages below.
blocks.zh: EKA评估正在进行的任务流中的索赔。 在连续假设测试(Wald,1992年)和真理维护(Doyle,1979年)的启发下,我们保留了合格但未经充分证实的主张,并更新其证据,因为随后的轨迹提供了支持或反对。 EKA从下面的阶段开始。

blocks.en: 4.4.1 Atomization

An extractor output may bundle multiple claims within a single item. Admitting or rejecting such an item as a whole using EKA might let the unsupported part into context or discard the supported part.
Inspired by atomic decomposition ( Min et al., 2023 ) , we use an atomizer across all four knowledge types, splitting claims only when their components are self-contained and independent. Each resulting atom must be grounded in the environment feedback relevant to its own content, either directly or, for second-order knowledge, through its first-order claims. The atomic claims serve as the basic units for relation judgment and evidence accumulation. We denote those extracted from batch B j B_{j} by U j = { u 1 , … , u | U j | } U_{j}=\{u_{1},\ldots,u_{|U_{j}|}\} . Appendix C reports technical details including prompts and output schemas.

在原子分解(Min等人,2023年)的启发下,我们使用一种涵盖所有四种知识类型的原子分解器,只有当其成分自成一体且独立时,才分割主张. 所产生的每个原子必须基于与其本身内容相关的环境反馈,要么直接提供,要么通过一阶要求获得二阶知识。 原子主张是关系判断和证据积累的基本单位. 我们用U j = {u 1,., u j | } 、\ ldots, u _{| j } 来表示从批B j B _{j } 取自 U j = {u 1, ... u j } 的 。 附 录 C报告技术细节,包括提示和产出计划。

blocks.en: 4.4.2 Claim Routing and Relation Judgment
blocks.zh: 4.4.2 索赔程序与关系判决

blocks.en: A routing agent examines each atomic claim u u , its cited environment-feedback spans, and the explanation linking them. A claim is directly grounded if the cited feedback itself states the claim under its stated scope, and indirectly grounded if it follows from such feedback through inference or abstraction, possibly via its first-order parent claims; claims with neither are excluded. The grounding type determines the admission route. Directly grounded claims follow the immediate admission path, since the feedback already establishes them. Indirectly grounded claims follow the deferred admission path, since their full scope still requires corroboration, for example because of causal attribution or conditions beyond those observed. We denote the route by z ⁡ ( u ) ∈ { Immediate , Deferred } . z(u)\in\{\textsc{Immediate},\textsc{Deferred}\}. The route depends on whether the evidence covers a claim’s scope, not on its knowledge type. A factual claim such as “schema versions use completed as the finalized label” is deferred, since an observation from version 1 does not cover its cross-version scope. Conversely, a conceptual claim can be admitted immediately when it only relates directly observed facts within their observed scope, such as “timestamp encodings differ across fdbk_g1 , fdbk_g2 , and fdbk_g3 ”. Routing decisions are recorded when extracted claims are integrated into the persistent state.

Inspired by natural-logic approaches to textual inference ( MacCartney and Manning, 2007 ) , we compare each new extracted claim with existing claims. For a new extracted claim u u and an existing claim v v , the relation judge predicts one or more material logical relations r ⁡ ( u , v ) ⊆ ℛ r(u,v)\subseteq\mathcal{R} between u u and v v .
We define ℛ \mathcal{R} to contain Equivalent , Specialize , Generalize , Contradict , Overlap , and Independent . The relations are defined as follows: • Equivalent : u u and v v entail each other under the same scope. • Specialize : The new claim u u entails the broader stored claim v v . • Generalize : The stored claim v v entails the broader new claim u u . • Contradict : The claims cover overlapping scope but cannot both hold. • Overlap : Shared content without entailment or contradiction. • Independent : No logical relationship. These judgments determine how subsequent experience supports or challenges stored claims.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en: We find that approximately 12–33% of entries retained by existing experience-reuse systems harm subsequent task performance. To address this, we propose RIKA, which combines hierarchical extraction of four knowledge types with EKA, admitting claims as evidence accumulates from the task stream without additional validation tasks. RIKA achieves the highest aggregate score on every backbone across six task streams, and EKA also improves SkillOpt and Trace2Skill.
blocks.zh: 我们发现,现有经验再利用系统所保留的条目约有12-33%损害随后的任务业绩。 为了解决这一问题,我们提议RIKA, 将四类知识的分级取出与EKA相结合,接受索赔作为从任务流中积累的证据,而不增加审定任务。 RIKA在6个任务流的每个骨干上都取得了最高的总分分,而EKA还改进了SkillOpt和Trace2Skill.

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Our empirical study focuses on six text-based, tool-mediated task streams and four model backbones. Although the streams span heterogeneous domains and interaction patterns, the results may not directly transfer to more diverse settings, where experience also includes perceptual or physical feedback. In addition, we study continual learning through an external knowledge artifact while keeping the underlying model parameters fixed. How hierarchical extraction and evidence-based admission interact with parameter-updating approaches remains an open direction.
blocks.zh: 我们的经验研究侧重于6个以文字为基础的、以工具为媒介的任务流和4个模型骨干。 虽然这些流跨越了不同的领域和互动模式,但结果可能不会被直接转移到更多样化的场合,在那里,经验还包括感知或物理反馈. 此外,我们研究通过外部知识文物不断学习,同时保持基本模型参数的固定。 分级提取和基于证据的承认如何与参数更新方法相互作用仍然是一个开放的方向。

blocks.en: Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en: Agent trajectories may contain personal information that could persist in the knowledge file, so deployment on real user interactions would require filtering or anonymizing trajectories first; our experiments use benchmarks without real personal data. Finally, our evaluation covers six text-based, tool-mediated task streams and four model backbones, and it does not show that RIKA is safe for high-stakes domains such as medicine, law, or finance, where domain-specific validation and human oversight would be required.
blocks.zh: 代理轨迹可能包含在知识文件中可能持续存在的个人信息,因此在实际用户互动上的部署需要先过滤或匿名轨迹;我们的实验使用没有真实个人数据的基准. 最后,我们的评价包括6个基于文本、工具中介的任务流和4个示范骨干,它没有显示RIKA对于医学、法律或金融等需要特定领域验证和人力监督的高考领域是安全的。

blocks.en: C.1 Prompt Templates and Output Schemas
blocks.zh: C.1 快速模板和输出图

blocks.en: All extracted claims must be grounded, directly or indirectly, in environment feedback contained in the source trajectories. Here, environment feedback includes environment observations, tool outputs, errors, and task outcomes. Each candidate must identify the relevant feedback and its connection to the claim; actions and agent reasoning provide context but do not independently justify extraction. Indirect grounding may involve inference or abstraction through factual or procedural claims, but must remain traceable to the original feedback. Claims without such a connection are excluded before admission routing.
blocks.zh: 所有提取的索赔必须直接或间接地以来源轨迹中的环境反馈为依据。 在这方面,环境反馈包括环境观测、工具产出、错误和任务结果。 每个候选人必须确定有关的反馈及其与索赔的联系;行动和代理人推理提供背景,但不能独立地证明提取是合理的。 间接依据可能涉及通过事实或程序主张推论或抽象,但必须能够追踪原始反馈。 没有这种联系的索赔在入院前不包括在内。

blocks.en: Each extractor receives the following common instruction, followed by a type-specific objective: Extract only reusable claims that have a direct or indirect grounding in environment feedback in the supplied trajectories. Environment feedback includes environment observations, tool outputs, errors, and task outcomes. Start from this feedback and identify what it establishes or reasonably suggests. Actions, plans, and agent reasoning may provide context, but cannot independently ground a claim; do not extract generic knowledge merely because it appears in the trajectory. For every claim, cite the minimal feedback spans, mark the grounding as direct or indirect, and explain the connection. For indirect claims, state the inference or abstraction and what remains unverified; trace any first-order parent claims back to their original feedback. Write self-contained claims whose scope states the task, entities, conditions, and environment version needed for reuse. Preserve uncertainty and exceptions. Do not infer success from an attempted action or present a hypothesis as an observed fact. Exclude every claim without this feedback connection. Return an empty list if no eligible reusable claim exists.
blocks.zh: 每个提取器都得到以下共同指示,然后是特定类型的目标: 在所提供轨迹中,只提取在环境反馈中具有直接或间接基础的可重复使用的索赔。 环境反馈包括环境观测、工具产出、错误和任务结果。 从这一反馈开始,确定它确定或合理建议的内容。 行动、计划和代理人推理可以提供上下文,但不能独立地为索赔提供依据;不能仅仅因为它出现在轨迹中而获取一般知识。 对于每一项索赔,请引用最低反馈跨度,标出地基为直接或间接,并解释联系。 对于间接索赔,请说明推断或抽象,以及哪些尚未核实;追踪任何一等母索赔,以追溯到最初的反馈。 撰写自成一体的主张,其范围规定了重复使用所需的任务、实体、条件和环境版本。 保留不确定性和例外。 不要从企图采取的行动中推断成功与否,或提出假设作为观察到的事实。 排除没有此反馈连接的每条声明 。 如果不存在合格的可重复使用索赔,则返回空列表。

blocks.en: The factual and procedural extractors receive a serialized trajectories field. The conceptual extractor additionally receives factual_items , and the metacognitive extractor additionally receives procedural_items . These first-order items include their IDs, scopes, feedback spans, grounding explanations, and provenance fields.
blocks.zh: 事实取出器和程序取出器得到一个序列化的出轨场. 概念提取器额外接收事实性项目,元识别提取器额外接收程序性项目。 这些一等物品包括身份证、范围、反馈跨度、地面解释和出处。

blocks.en: The four type-specific objectives are: • Factual extractor: identify concrete properties of entities, schemas, states, tool behavior, feedback, and observed outcomes. Cite the environment feedback establishing or suggesting each property, and keep statements tied to the versions and conditions actually observed. • Procedural extractor: identify executable operations or workflows whose behavior is grounded in environment feedback in the trajectories. Specify ordered actions, required inputs or tools, prerequisites, expected outputs, and observed failure-recovery steps. Link the relevant actions to observed tool outputs, errors, or outcomes. Action sequences alone do not qualify. Do not claim that a procedure is generally effective merely because it appeared in a successful trajectory. • Conceptual extractor: given the trajectories and extracted factual claims, identify relations or regularities that organize multiple facts. Each conceptual claim must cite the factual claim IDs on which it depends, trace them to the original feedback, and explain the abstraction connecting that feedback to the claim. It must not merely restate one fact. • Metacognitive extractor: given the trajectories and extracted procedural claims, identify evidence-grounded guidance about when to select, avoid, monitor, or revise a procedure. Each metacognitive claim must cite the procedural claim IDs on which it depends, trace them to the original feedback, and explain how the observed success, failure, or recovery motivates the guidance.
blocks.zh: 四个特定类型的目标是: • 事实提取器:识别实体的具体属性,计划,状态,工具行为,反馈,以及所观察到的结果. 输入建立或建议每个属性的环境反馈,并保持声明与版本和条件的链接,实际观察。 • 程序提取器:识别其行为基于轨道环境反馈的可执行操作或工作流程。 指定命令的行动、所需投入或工具、先决条件、预期产出和观察到的故障回收步骤。 将相关行动与观察到的工具输出、错误或结果相链接。 单是动作序列没有资格。 不要仅仅因为程序出现在成功的轨道上就声称程序一般是有效的。 二. 支助 概念提取器:考虑到轨迹和提取的事实主张,确定组织多种事实的关系或规律。 每项概念性索赔必须引用它所依赖的事实性索赔的ID,追踪到原始反馈,并解释将这种反馈与索赔联系起来的抽象。 它决不能仅仅重复一个事实。 二. 支助 变相提取器:考虑到轨迹和提取出的程序索赔,确定关于何时选择、避免、监测或修订程序的证据依据指南。 每个元识别索赔必须引用它所依赖的程序索赔ID,追踪到原始反馈,并解释观察到的成功、失败或恢复如何激励指导。

blocks.en: Each extracted item follows a shared field-level schema: • id , type , and claim : a local identifier, one of the four knowledge types, and a self-contained claim. • scope : the task family, entities, conditions, prerequisites, and environment or schema version under which the claim is stated. • source_trajectories and evidence_spans : immutable trajectory IDs and the minimal environment-feedback spans grounding the claim; action or reasoning context may accompany but cannot replace those spans. • grounding_type and grounding_explanation : direct or indirect grounding, and a short explanation linking the cited feedback to the exact claim, including any inference, abstraction, or unverified extension. • parent_ids : empty for first-order factual and procedural claims; factual IDs for conceptual claims; and procedural IDs for metacognitive claims.

blocks.en: The atomizer is conditioned on the knowledge type and receives one extracted claim at a time: Decompose the extracted claim into the smallest claims that can each stand alone and be reused independently. Split conjunctions only when each part remains meaningful with its own scope and evidence. Do not split inseparable steps, remove qualifiers, broaden scope, or introduce new content. For each atom, retain only the feedback spans that ground that atom, preserve the relevant parent lineage, and update the direct or indirect grounding explanation. Exclude an atom if no feedback span directly or indirectly grounds it. If the extracted claim is already atomic and feedback-grounded, return it unchanged. For each output atomic claim, the schema contains atom_id , parent_id , type , claim , scope , source_trajectories , evidence_spans , grounding_type , and grounding_explanation .
blocks.zh: 原子化器以知识类型为条件,一次收到一个提取的债权: 将提取的债权分解为最小的债权,每个债权可以独立独立独立地再使用. 只有在每一部分仍然有意义,而且有自己的范围和证据时,才将组合分开。 不分割不可分割的步骤,删除限定词,拓宽范围,或引入新内容. 对于每个原子,只保留该原子底部的反馈,保留相关的母系,并更新直接或间接的地基解释. 如果一个原子没有反馈,则排除它。 如果提取的索赔已经是原子和反馈依据,则不作修改地返回。 对于每个输出原子主张,计划包含原子_id,母体_id,类型,主张,范围,出处_外出,证据_spans,地基_类型,地基_解释.

blocks.en: For every eligible atomic claim, the router receives the claim, its cited environment-feedback spans, and its grounding explanation: First verify that the claim has a direct or indirect connection to the cited environment feedback. Exclude a claim lacking this connection rather than routing it to Deferred . For an eligible claim, decide whether that feedback establishes the exact claim under its stated scope. Route it to Immediate only when environment observations, tool outputs, or explicit feedback are sufficient without extrapolation, assumed causality, or unavailable information. Route it to Deferred only when it is a feedback-grounded inference or generalization whose full scope needs corroboration, such as an extrapolation beyond the observed conditions or a causal interpretation not yet isolated. Knowledge type alone must not determine the route. For eligible claims, the router returns atom_id , route , witness_trajectory_ids , witness_spans , and a short justification identifying either the direct warrant or both the feedback basis and the extension still requiring support.
blocks.zh: 对于每一个符合条件的原子索赔,路由器都会收到索赔,其引用的环境反馈跨度,以及其基础解释: 首先核实索赔与所引用的环境反馈有直接或间接的联系。 不包括一项缺乏这种连接而不是将其引向被推迟的索赔。 对于符合资格的索赔,决定该反馈是否证实其规定范围内的确切索赔。 只有当环境观测、工具输出或明确反馈都足够,而且没有推断、假定的因果关系或没有信息时,才能立即进行。 只有当其范围完全需要确证的反馈依据推论或概括,例如超出观察条件的推论或尚未孤立的因果关系解释时,才将其推迟。 知识类型本身不能决定路线。 对于符合条件的诉求,路由器返回原子_id,路由,见证_trajectory_ids,见证_spans,以及一个简短的理由,说明直接授权令或者反馈基础和仍然需要支持的扩展.

blocks.en: The relation judge receives a new atomic claim and relevant canonical claims from the persistent state: Compare the claims under their explicit scopes. Return every material relation among Equivalent , Specialize , Generalize , Contradict , Overlap , and Independent . Treat two claims as equivalent only if they entail each other under the same scope. For directional entailment, identify which claim is more specific. Mark contradiction only when the scopes overlap and both claims cannot hold there. Shared vocabulary alone is not a relation. Cite the phrases and scope conditions that determine the judgment; do not alter either claim. Each judgment contains new_id , stored_id , a set relations , entailment_direction when applicable, overlap_scope , and rationale . These judgments feed into the evidence-count and admission updates specified in Table 7 .
blocks.zh: 关系法官收到来自持续状态的新的原子要求和相关神话要求: 比较其明确范围内的索赔。 回归所有物质关系 等价,专业,概括,矛盾,重叠,独立 将两项索赔作为等同索赔处理,条件是它们相互之间属于同一范围。 对于方向性索赔,确定哪些索赔更为具体。 只有当范围重叠,而且两项要求都无法坚持时,才标出矛盾。 单独共享词汇不是关系. 标出决定判决的短语和范围条件;不改变任何一项要求。 每个判断都包含新“id”、存储“id”、设定关系、在适用情况下包含“方向”、重叠“范围”和“原理”。 这些判决纳入了表7所列明的证据计算和承认情况更新。

blocks.en: Rendering programmatically concatenates the admitted claims. After each batch, admission is recomputed with thresholds of 1 1 for immediate claims and k k for deferred claims. The program groups all currently admitted claims under the four knowledge-type headings and serializes each canonical claim once as a scoped bullet, as described in Appendix D.5 . Stored claim text and its scope, prerequisites, exceptions, and environment version are preserved; internal IDs, evidence counts, provenance, routing decisions, and relation labels are omitted. Empty type headings are omitted. The resulting document replaces the previous knowledge block at each batch boundary.
blocks.zh: 从方案上对已受理的债权进行整理。 在每批索赔之后,接纳的门槛值为:即时索赔为11;推迟索赔为kk。 如附录D.5所述,该方案将目前受理的四类知识类索赔归为一类,并将每件犬类索赔一次作为范围标注。 保留了存储的索赔文本及其范围、先决条件、例外和环境版本;省略了内部的ID、证据清点、出处、路由决定以及关系标签。 空类型标题被省略 。 由此产生的文档取代了每个分批边界上以前的知识块.

blocks.en: C.2 End-to-End Worked Example
blocks.zh: C.2 最终工作实例

blocks.en: The following stylized DB example illustrates the information flow across three successive batches, each containing one relevant trajectory, with k = 3 k=3 .
blocks.zh: 以下分级的DB示例说明了连续三个批次的信息流,每个批次包含一个相关轨迹,其中k=3克=3.

blocks.en: In the first batch, τ a \tau_{a} inspects schema version 1 and observes an orders(status, amount) table with completed and pending orders. For a realized-revenue query, summing all matching orders gives an incorrect answer, whereas filtering status = completed gives the correct answer. In the second batch, τ b \tau_{b} observes the same contrast on different order records under another query condition in version 1. Neither trajectory involves a schema change. blocks.en: We evaluate continual adaptation on six ordered task streams from Continual Learning Bench ( Asawa et al., 2026 ) : • Blind Spectrum Monitoring ( BSM ) contains 90 scans divided into three fixed stages of 30 scans each. Stage order and boundaries remain fixed across runs. Repeated runs permute instances only within stages, except for Sales , whose chronological order is preserved in every run.

blocks.zh: G.2 关于结构组成部分的考虑

blocks.en: We ablate three supporting mechanisms in RIKA: atomization, claim forgetting, and state-based rendering.
blocks.zh: 我们放弃了RIKA的三个支持机制:原子分解、声称忘记和基于国家的渲染。

blocks.en: As shown in Table 17 , removing any of these components consistently reduces performance. Without atomization, scores drop by 0.014 0.014 – 0.017 0.017 on DB and COHORT, reflecting less precise relation matching over compound claims. Disabling forgetting also degrades performance, as stale unsupported pending claims accumulate in the state. Finally, replacing state-based rendering with incremental rewriting yields further drops, including 0.032 0.032 on DB , showing the benefit of regenerating the knowledge file from the current accumulation state rather than repeatedly editing previous text.
blocks.zh: 如表17所示,删除其中任何构成部分都始终会降低业绩。 没有原子化,DB和COHORT的分数就下降了0.014 0.014 -- -- 0.017 0.017,反映出与复合索赔相比关系不准确。 使人无法忘却也会降低性能,因为呆滞的无凭据的未决索赔在州内累积. 最后,将基于状态的渲染替换为递增重写产生出进一步的下降,包括DB上的0.032 0.032,显示了从当前积累状态中重新生成知识文件的好处,而不是再三地编辑以前的文本.
